info.title: Djinn
info.description:
The public methods of Djinn, generated from the protos in `api/` (`go tool task gen`). They are the commands of
the `djinn` command line and the tools of `djinn mcp`: `QuestionService/Answer` is `djinn question answer`.

Each method speaks the [Connect protocol](https://connectrpc.com/docs/protocol): a `POST` with
`Content-Type: application/json`, the request in protobuf JSON as the body. `djinn up` writes its address in
`server.addr` of the data directory. On macOS and Linux it is a Unix socket:
`curl --unix-socket <data>/djinn.sock http://localhost/plan.v1.ProjectService/List -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'`.
On Windows or with `djinn up --browser` it is `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/?token=…`, whose token goes in an
`Authorization: Bearer` header.

A method that only reads changes nothing, and Connect serves it as a `GET` too, the request in the query:
`GET /plan.v1.ProjectService/List?encoding=json&message=%7B%7D`.

The streaming methods (`GateService/Hold`, `WishService/Watch`, `TaskService/Watch`) use Connect's streaming
protocol: `Content-Type: application/connect+json`, each message in an envelope of 5 bytes, a flag and its length.

recommendation.title: recommendation
recommendation.description: The option you recommend now, and why; the former recommendation when empty.

wishId.title: wish_id
wishId.description: Wish of the question, needed only when its code exists in several wishes.

cpuPercent.title: cpu_percent
cpuPercent.description: CPU used since the reading before, in percent of one core: 200 is two cores busy.

memoryBytes.title: memory_bytes
memoryBytes.description:
Resident memory, in bytes: the sum over its processes, a page they share counted once per process. From a
 cgroup, what the kernel charges it (memory.current): its processes' memory once, and the page cache they filled.

peakCpuPercent.title: peak_cpu_percent
peakCpuPercent.description: Highest cpu_percent read, over all the task's workers.

peakMemoryBytes.title: peak_memory_bytes
peakMemoryBytes.description: Highest memory_bytes read, or held between two readings (a cgroup's memory.peak), over all the task's workers.

plan.v1.Resources.title: Resources
plan.v1.Resources.description:
Resources is what a task's worker uses of the machine: its process group and every process it started, even one
 that left the group. Linux reads the cgroup of the worker's systemd scope when it runs in one, else /proc; macOS,
 ps.

note.title: note
note.description: For a request, what to dig into.

context.title: context
context.description: For a revision, what the question said before it.

options.title: options
options.description: For a revision, the options before it.

recommendation.title: recommendation
recommendation.description: For a revision, the recommendation before it.

plan.v1.Round.title: Round
plan.v1.Round.description: A round of a question before it is decided: a request to investigate, or the lead's revision.

request.title: request
request.description: The request, as it was said.

fromWishId.title: from_wish_id
fromWishId.description: The wish the request came to; it is proposed last, to keep the request there.

options.title: options
options.description: The destinations, the recommended one first.

plan.v1.Route.title: Route
plan.v1.Route.description:
Route is where Djinn proposes to send a request that is not about the wish it came to: into an existing wish, or
 into a new one. Djinn computes it without a model, from the wishes' titles, their projects and their latest
 blocks.

plan.v1.RouteKind.title: RouteKind
plan.v1.RouteKind.description: RouteKind is what a destination of a request does.

wishId.title: wish_id
wishId.description: The wish to file the request in; empty for a new wish.

title.title: title
title.description: The title of that wish, or the title proposed for the new one.

projectIds.title: project_ids
projectIds.description: The projects of the new wish.

pauseWishId.title: pause_wish_id
pauseWishId.description: The active wish paused to make room, for a swap.

score.title: score
score.description: How close the wish is to the request: higher is closer. 0 for a new wish.

template.title: template
template.description:
The skill whose wish template the request matched, for a new wish: its title comes from it, its watcher starts
 with it, and its lead starts with the skill.

plan.v1.RouteOption.title: RouteOption
plan.v1.RouteOption.description: RouteOption is one destination of a request.

plan.v1.SettingSource.title: SettingSource
plan.v1.SettingSource.description: SettingSource is where a project setting comes from.

project.title: project
project.description: The project that uses the skill.

source.title: source
source.description: Where a summoned skill comes from, as <project>/<skill>; empty for the project's own.

directory.title: directory
directory.description: Its folder on this machine, in the project that holds it.

description.title: description
description.description: What it does, from its SKILL.md.

missing.title: missing
missing.description: Why a summoned skill cannot be found; empty when it is.

template.title: template
template.description:
The title of the wish template its SKILL.md declares (metadata.djinn.wish), placeholders and all; empty without
 one.

templateError.title: template_error
templateError.description: Why its wish template cannot be used; empty when it can, or without one.

inboxSource.title: inbox_source
inboxSource.description: The command line of the inbox source its SKILL.md declares (metadata.djinn.source); empty without one.

inboxSourceError.title: inbox_source_error
inboxSourceError.description: Why its inbox source cannot be used; empty when it can, or without one.

plan.v1.Skill.title: Skill
plan.v1.Skill.description: A skill as a project sees it: its own, or summoned from another project.

project.title: project
project.description: Only the skills of this project, by name or identifier.

skills.title: skills
skills.description: The skills, by project then name.

skill.title: skill
skill.description: The skill, as <project>/<skill>: the project that holds it, then its folder name. Case ignored.

into.title: into
into.description: The project that summons it, by name or identifier.

skill.title: skill
skill.description: The skill, as the project now sees it.

skill.title: skill
skill.description: The skill, as <project>/<skill>, as it was summoned. Case ignored.

from.title: from
from.description: The project that summoned it, by name or identifier.

projectId.title: project_id
projectId.description: The project that holds the skill.

skill.title: skill
skill.description: The skill's folder name, in that project's .agents/skills or .claude/skills.

plan.v1.Summon.title: Summon
plan.v1.Summon.description:
A skill a project summons from another project. It stays in its source, and the summoning project follows it:
 Djinn shows each worker the source's folder as it is, by its agent's own path, and writes nothing in the project.

projectId.title: project_id
projectId.description: Project the task works in; empty for a task outside any project, which only reads.

code.title: code
code.description: Short code to dictate, like W2, unique within the wish.

provider.title: provider
provider.description: Kind of agent that works on the task.

worktree.title: worktree
worktree.description:
Root of the task's Git worktree, in Djinn's data folder; empty outside Git, where the worker runs in the
 project folder.

sessionId.title: session_id
sessionId.description: Session of the agent, to resume it.

usage.title: usage
usage.description: What the worker spent so far, summed over its runs.

exitCode.title: exit_code
exitCode.description: Exit code of the worker's process, once it ended.

error.title: error
error.description: Why the task failed or stopped.

access.title: access
access.description: Where its worker's rights come from.

editQuestionId.title: edit_question_id
editQuestionId.description:
The question asking the developer whether the worker may edit the project's files, for a task whose access
 is, or was, ASKING.

model.title: model
model.description: Model of the agent, as spawned; empty for the provider's default. A worker started again keeps it.

maxBudgetUsd.title: max_budget_usd
maxBudgetUsd.description: Most the task may spend, in US dollars, over all its runs; 0 for no cap.

dependsOn.title: depends_on
dependsOn.description:
Tasks that must be done before this one starts, by identifier. A task whose dependency ends without being done
 fails too.

writeScopes.title: write_scopes
writeScopes.description:
What the task writes, as paths in the project's folder ("src", "docs/api.md"); empty for the whole folder.
 Outside Git, two tasks whose scopes overlap never run together. In Git, each task has its own worktree, and
 scopes are not checked.

scheduled.title: scheduled
scheduled.description:
Djinn starts the task's worker by itself, once its dependencies are done, its scopes free and a slot free:
 the task was spawned or planned on this machine. A task imported with a wish is not.

waitReason.title: wait_reason
waitReason.description: Why a planned task has not started yet; empty once it has.

forkSession.title: fork_session
forkSession.description:
The session the worker started from, forked: a copy of another task's or of the lead's conversation, with a
 new session of its own. Empty for a worker that starts from its prompt alone, the default. Stays on this
 machine: an export leaves it out.

forkOf.title: fork_of
forkOf.description: Where the fork comes from, for a reader: the code of the task (W1), or "lead".

resumeAfter.title: resume_after
resumeAfter.description:
When a RESUMING task may start again: after its provider's usage limit resets. While it is ahead, no new worker
 of that provider starts. Unset: as soon as the scheduler can.

resumes.title: resumes
resumes.description: How many times Djinn resumed the task by itself. At 3, a task cut short again fails instead.

restart.title: restart
restart.description: A watcher's command starts again after each exit, until the task is stopped (djinn task spawn --restart).

lastLine.title: last_line
lastLine.description:
The first line of the last paragraph a watcher's command printed, as its wish's lead was told. Empty for an
 agent.

closed.title: closed
closed.description:
Who marked the task done by hand, when and why (TaskService.Done), or which fork continues it. Empty for a task
 its worker finished.

continuing.title: continuing
continuing.description:
The task was continued (TaskService.Continue): its next worker resumes its own session on the last prompt of its
 events, instead of being told Djinn restarted. Cleared as that worker starts.

decision.title: decision
decision.description:
The decision the task comes from (djinn task spawn --decision): a question's code (Q43), or the id of a block of
 kind decision. Empty for a task no decision led to.

resources.title: resources
resources.description:
What its worker uses of the machine, read every few seconds while it runs: the latest reading and the peaks over
 all its workers. Absent until a reading, and where Djinn does not measure workers (Windows, the fake agent).

kind.title: kind
kind.description: What the task is: work a worker does, the default, or an azima of the plan, which no worker ever runs.

partOf.title: part_of
partOf.description:
The azima the task is part of (an azima of its wish), by identifier; empty for none. A grouping, never a
 wait: only depends_on makes a task wait. The tasks of a wish, through depends_on and part_of together, form a
 graph without cycle.

planFile.title: plan_file
planFile.description:
For an azima read from a plan file (djinn plan sync): the file, as its project names it
 ("plan/8e8d3d76-orchestrator.md"), and its phase there ("2", "later"). Empty for an azima of no file.

azima.title: azima
azima.description: For an azima: where it stands, computed on every read from its parts and what it depends on, never stored.

integration.title: integration
integration.description:
Where the task's finished work stands on its way into its wish's integration branch: unset for a task whose work
 Djinn does not integrate (outside Git, an azima, a project that names no test command, not done).

tilasms.title: tilasms
tilasms.description:
The tilasms of the wish that cite it (djinn tilasm put --cites), by code (L01): computed on every read, never
 stored.

correction.title: correction
correction.description:
For a correction worker, which Djinn starts by itself when a batch's merge conflicts in code or its tests fail:
 what it corrects. Its worktree starts on the failed merge, and its branch integrates like any task's.

proofNeeds.title: proof_needs
proofNeeds.description:
For an azima read from a plan file (djinn plan sync): its Done-when boxes left unchecked for a proof no worker can
 give, box by box, when nothing else is left in them: every unchecked box says "(needs: …)", or holds boxes that
 do. Empty while a box without needs is unchecked (work is left), when every box is checked, and for a file
 without a Done-when section.

plan.v1.Task.title: Task
plan.v1.Task.description: A task is one item of a wish's flight plan, done in one project.

plan.v1.TaskAccess.title: TaskAccess
plan.v1.TaskAccess.description: TaskAccess says where the rights of a task's worker come from (docs/providers.md, "What a worker may do").

task.title: task
task.description: The task: its code (W6) or its identifier.

after.title: after
after.description: What comes before it: tasks of the same wish, by code or identifier; none for nothing.

plan.v1.TaskAfter.title: TaskAfter
plan.v1.TaskAfter.description: What one task waits for, in place of what it had.

failure.title: failure
failure.description: The failure, as its worktree starts from it.

attempt.title: attempt
attempt.description: Which attempt it is, from 1, for this failure: past the project's correction_attempts, Djinn asks the person.

plan.v1.TaskCorrection.title: TaskCorrection
plan.v1.TaskCorrection.description: TaskCorrection is what a correction worker corrects.

seq.title: seq
seq.description: Position in the task, from 1, with no gap.

text.title: text
text.description: The event for a reader: the text, the tool and its input, the error.

usage.title: usage
usage.description: What the worker spent so far, on a usage event.

raw.title: raw
raw.description: The provider's line as it came, when the event comes from one.

plan.v1.TaskEvent.title: TaskEvent
plan.v1.TaskEvent.description: An event of a task's worker: what it said, the tools it called, what it spent.

plan.v1.TaskEventKind.title: TaskEventKind
plan.v1.TaskEventKind.description: TaskEventKind says what a worker event is. Its content stays free text.

branch.title: branch
branch.description: The integration branch, in the task's project.

sha.title: sha
sha.description: For COMMITTED, the commit the branch moved to, with the task's work.

reason.title: reason
reason.description:
For CONFLICT and RED, what failed; for PENDING, why it waits, when it waits for something else than its batch; for
 COMMITTED with a correction worker's work, "corrected by W5".

failure.title: failure
failure.description:
For CONFLICT and RED, what failed, as a correction worker starts from it; unset when no worker can correct it
 (a command that could not run, a merge that failed without conflicts).

correctedBy.title: corrected_by
correctedBy.description: The correction worker that corrects the work, or did: for COMMITTED, the work went in with it ("corrected by W5").

attempts.title: attempts
attempts.description: How many correction workers were started for it in a row.

questionId.title: question_id
questionId.description: The question Djinn asked once the attempts were spent: try again, leave it, or the person takes it.

plan.v1.TaskIntegration.title: TaskIntegration
plan.v1.TaskIntegration.description:
TaskIntegration is where a task's finished work stands on its way into its wish's integration branch (T30). When a
 worker ends done, Djinn commits its worktree on its branch, merges it with the batch into the integration branch in
 a worktree of its own, makes the generated files again on a conflict only in them, tests the result through a gate,
 and moves the branch when it passes.

plan.v1.TaskKind.title: TaskKind
plan.v1.TaskKind.description: TaskKind says what a task is.

force.title: force
force.description: Remove the worktree even when it holds changes not committed.

prompt.title: prompt
prompt.description: What to ask its worker now, on its session.

by.title: by
by.description:
Who continues it; by default the lead. The window says developer.
enum.defined_only = true

task.title: task
task.description: The task, planned again: running, or waiting with its reason.

dependsOn.title: depends_on
dependsOn.description: Same as after, the name it had: kept so that what depends with --depends-on still works.

after.title: after
after.description:
What comes before the task: tasks of the same wish that must be done first, by code (W1, T07) or identifier.
 Repeat it, or separate them with commas: --after W1,W2. None leaves the task waiting for nothing.

also.title: also
also.description:
Other tasks of the wish whose dependencies are set in the same step, all or none: --also W6=W5,W3 sets what W6
 waits for, --also W7= clears it. The graph they make together has no cycle, or nothing changes.

also.title: also
also.description: The other tasks set (--also), in the order asked.

note.title: note
note.description: Why it is done, in a few words.

by.title: by
by.description:
Who closes it; by default the lead. The window says developer.
enum.defined_only = true

partOf.title: part_of
partOf.description: The azima: its code (T07) or its identifier. Empty: the task is part of no azima.

wishId.title: wish_id
wishId.description: Only the tasks of this wish.

projectId.title: project_id
projectId.description: Only the tasks in this project.

text.title: text
text.description: The message, as the worker reads it.

event.title: event
event.description: The message, as an event of the task.

title.title: title
title.description: What the task does, in a sentence.

projectId.title: project_id
projectId.description:
Project to work in; by default the wish's project, when it has only one. For a wish without any project, the
 task runs outside any project: read-only, in an empty folder of its own.

prompt.title: prompt
prompt.description: What to ask the worker; by default the title.

provider.title: provider
provider.description:
Kind of agent; by default claude.
enum.defined_only = true

model.title: model
model.description: Model of the agent; by default the provider's.

maxBudgetUsd.title: max_budget_usd
maxBudgetUsd.description: Most the worker may spend, in US dollars, when the provider can enforce it.

dependsOn.title: depends_on
dependsOn.description: Same as after, the name it had: kept so that what spawns with --depends-on still works.

writeScopes.title: write_scopes
writeScopes.description:
A path the task writes, in the project's folder; none for the whole folder. Outside Git, tasks whose scopes
 overlap never run together.

later.title: later
later.description: Only plan the task: the call returns at once, and djinn up starts the worker when the task is ready.

fork.title: fork
fork.description:
Start the worker from a copy of this task's conversation (its code, W1, or its identifier), with a session of
 its own, instead of from the prompt alone. The inherited context is read again at every turn: prefer a short
 prompt, the default. Claude and Codex fork; Antigravity cannot.

fromLead.title: from_lead
fromLead.description: Start the worker from a copy of the lead's conversation, as --fork does from a task.

restart.title: restart
restart.description: For a watcher (--provider watch): start its command again after each exit, until the task is stopped.

decision.title: decision
decision.description:
The decision the task comes from: an answered question's code (Q43), or the id of a block of kind decision. The
 decision log links to the task, and the task to its decision.

partOf.title: part_of
partOf.description:
The azima the task belongs to: its code (T07) or its identifier. A grouping, never a wait: say what the task
 waits for with after.

kind.title: kind
kind.description:
What the task is; by default work, for a worker. azima makes an azima (T1, T2…): no worker, no prompt, never
 scheduled; work is spawned part of it.
enum.defined_only = true

after.title: after
after.description:
What comes before the task: tasks of the same wish that must be done first, by code (W1, T07) or identifier.
 Repeat it, or separate them with commas: --after W1,W2. Give a task what comes before it here, at its spawn.

blocks.title: blocks
blocks.description:
What comes after the task: planned tasks of the same wish, by code or identifier, that wait for it from now on.
 Each one gets the new task as one more dependency, in the same step as the spawn, so that no scheduler pass
 starts it in between. Refused for a task that has started (running, paused, done…) and for one that would close
 a cycle. Repeat it, or separate them with commas: --blocks W5,W6.

tilasm.title: tilasm
tilasm.description:
A tilasm of the wish given to the worker as context, by code (L01) or identifier: the worker's first prompt holds
 its text and the folder of its files. Repeat it, or separate them with commas: --tilasm L01,L02.

task.title: task
task.description: The task: running, or waiting with its reason.

afterSeq.title: after_seq
afterSeq.description: Only the events after this position, to resume where a reader left off.

raw.title: raw
raw.description: Also send each event's raw line from the provider.

plan.v1.TaskStatus.title: TaskStatus
plan.v1.TaskStatus.description: TaskStatus is where a task stands.

id.title: id
id.description: Identifier, a UUIDv7. Its links name it: djinn://tilasm/<id>.

code.title: code
code.description: Short code to dictate, like L01, unique within the wish.

author.title: author
author.description: Who made it: a task's code (W12), the lead, the developer.

versions.title: versions
versions.description: Its versions, the first first; the last one is the tilasm as its links show it.

cites.title: cites
cites.description: The azimas and tasks of the wish it explains, by identifier.

updateTime.title: update_time
updateTime.description: When its last version was put.

maxBytes.title: max_bytes
maxBytes.description: Most a version may hold, in bytes, its files summed: a put beyond it is refused, saying so.

plan.v1.Tilasm.title: Tilasm
plan.v1.Tilasm.description:
A tilasm is the material that explains a wish: a concept drawn, a data model walked through, a comparison laid out.
 A folder with an index.html and its sources, kept in Djinn's data folder, tilasms/<id>/v<n>/, never in a project.
 Putting it again adds a version; the latest is what its links show. The word comes from the Arabic ṭilasm, the
 origin of "talisman".

plan.v1.TilasmRef.title: TilasmRef
plan.v1.TilasmRef.description: TilasmRef points to a tilasm by its code or by its identifier.

tilasm.title: tilasm
tilasm.description: The tilasm: its code (L01) or its identifier.

wish.title: wish
wish.description: The wish, when a code is given and several wishes have it.

file.title: file
file.description:
The .zip to write; a relative path starts from the current directory. By default, the tilasm's title with .zip in
 the Downloads folder.

tilasm.title: tilasm
tilasm.description: The tilasm: its code (L01) or its identifier.

wish.title: wish
wish.description: The wish, when a code is given and several wishes have it.

version.title: version
version.description: An earlier version to read; by default the latest.

text.title: text
text.description: The text of its index.html, without tags, scripts nor styles.

directory.title: directory
directory.description: The folder of the version's files.

files.title: files
files.description: Its files, relative to that folder, with forward slashes.

link.title: link
link.description:
Its link, djinn://tilasm/<id>: it opens the tilasm in the app from a browser, a chat, a terminal or a Markdown
 file. Cite it so.

url.title: url
url.description:
The local http address of its latest version, for a browser or an agent that wants the HTML, while this Djinn
 runs: given when djinn up serves http (--browser, and on Windows). Empty while it listens on a socket only (the
 window on macOS and Linux): read the files in its folder then.

tilasm.title: tilasm
tilasm.description: The tilasm: its code (L01) or its identifier.

wish.title: wish
wish.description: The wish, when a code is given and several wishes have it.

directory.title: directory
directory.description: The tilasm's folder: version n is in its folder v<n>.

file.title: file
file.description: The .zip to import, as djinn tilasm export writes it; a relative path starts from the current directory.

wish.title: wish
wish.description: The wish to import it into.

author.title: author
author.description: Who imports it; the author of the file's tilasm by default.

tilasm.title: tilasm
tilasm.description: The tilasm, its new version last.

wish.title: wish
wish.description: Only the tilasms of this wish.

search.title: search
search.description:
Words to find, case ignored, in the code, the title or the text of the latest version; "talisman" or "tilasm"
 alone finds them all.

tilasms.title: tilasms
tilasms.description: The tilasms, by wish then code.

tilasm.title: tilasm
tilasm.description: The tilasm: its code (L01) or its identifier.

wish.title: wish
wish.description: The wish, when a code is given and several wishes have it.

window.title: window
window.description: A native window was brought to the front; false in browser mode, where the page shows it.

path.title: path
path.description: The folder that holds the index.html, or a .zip of it; a relative path starts from the current directory.

title.title: title
title.description:
Title, in a line; by default the <title> of its index.html, or the folder's name. A new version keeps the title
 it had unless one is given.

code.title: code
code.description: The tilasm to put again, by its code (L01): a new version of it. Without it, a new tilasm with the next code.

cites.title: cites
cites.description:
An azima or a task of the wish it explains, by code (T29, W12) or identifier; repeat it for each. A new version
 keeps what it cited unless some are given.

author.title: author
author.description: Who makes it: your task's code (W12) for a worker; lead by default.

tilasm.title: tilasm
tilasm.description: The tilasm, its new version last.

directory.title: directory
directory.description: The folder of the version put.

tilasm.title: tilasm
tilasm.description: The tilasm: its code (L01) or its identifier.

wish.title: wish
wish.description: The wish, when a code is given and several wishes have it.

author.title: author
author.description: Who restores it; lead by default.

tilasm.title: tilasm
tilasm.description: The tilasm, the restored version last.

restoredFrom.title: restored_from
restoredFrom.description: The version it copies, when it was restored from an earlier one; 0 otherwise.

plan.v1.TilasmVersion.title: TilasmVersion
plan.v1.TilasmVersion.description: TilasmVersion is one put of a tilasm: its files stay in tilasms/<id>/v<number>/.

cacheReadTokens.title: cache_read_tokens
cacheReadTokens.description: Tokens read from the prompt cache.

cacheWriteTokens.title: cache_write_tokens
cacheWriteTokens.description: Tokens written to the prompt cache.

costUsd.title: cost_usd
costUsd.description: Cost in US dollars, as the provider computes it.

plan.v1.Usage.title: Usage
plan.v1.Usage.description: Usage is what a worker spent, as its provider reports it.

title.title: title
title.description: What is wished, in a sentence.

allowances.title: allowances
allowances.description: Rights the developer allows the wish's workers, per project, ahead of any task.

lead.title: lead
lead.description: The lead: the agent session that drives the wish, for djinn wish resume to take it back.

state.title: state
state.description: Where the wish stands: active, paused or granted. Three wishes are active at most.

rank.title: rank
rank.description: Place among the active wishes, from 1: the first one has priority. 0 for a paused or granted wish.

grantTime.title: grant_time
grantTime.description: When the user granted the wish.

ready.title: ready
ready.description:
Djinn proposes to grant the wish: it has tasks, all finished, no question is open, and no task waits for an
 answer or failed. Computed on every read, never stored. Only the user grants a wish.

template.title: template
template.description: The skill the wish was made from, when a request matched its wish template; unset otherwise.

integrationBranches.title: integration_branches
integrationBranches.description:
The branch each Git project of the wish integrates its tasks' finished work into: by default the branch the
 project's checkout was on when the wish was made, or, for a wish made before Djinn recorded it, when its first
 task's work was to integrate (djinn wish set-integration).

commitAfterMinutes.title: commit_after_minutes
commitAfterMinutes.description:
Djinn commits the finished work into the integration branch when an azima ends, or once this many minutes have

 waits for is committed at once, alone. 0: 60 minutes, 3 tasks.

tags.name: TilasmService
tags.description:
Tilasms, or talismans: the material that explains a wish, kept on this machine and linked from anywhere. A put
 replaces a tilasm with a new version, and the earlier ones can be read and restored.

tags.name: QuestionService
tags.description: Questions agents ask, and the decisions taken.

tags.name: SkillService
tags.description:
Skills: what a project's agents know how to do, one folder each in the Agent Skills format (a SKILL.md, maybe
 scripts and references), in .agents/skills or .claude/skills. A project summons a skill of another project to
 use it without copying it: it follows its source.

tags.name: InboxService
tags.description:
The inbox: what comes from outside, proposed as requests. A source is a command a skill declares in its SKILL.md
 (metadata.djinn.source), run like a watcher, logged in by its own tool: Djinn holds no token. A source runs only
 once you plug it in, on this machine. Each paragraph it prints becomes an item with its proposed route; nothing is
 made until you answer.

tags.name: WishService
tags.description: Wishes: what you ask Djinn for, across projects.

tags.name: BlockService
tags.description: Blocks: the free content of a wish, beside its tasks and questions.

tags.name: MarkService
tags.description:
Marks: what the developer read or approved from the window, on questions, decisions and blocks, so that the lead
 acts on a click without a word.

tags.name: TaskService
tags.description: Tasks: one worker each, an agent process in the task's own worktree.

tags.name: PlanService
tags.description:
The plan of a wish as a graph of azimas: tasks of kind AZIMA that no worker runs, which work is part of. The store
 holds the graph; a project's plan/ folder holds one Markdown file per azima, for Git to carry.

tags.name: MachineService
tags.description: MachineService says what the machine has, how loaded it is, and how many workers Djinn runs on it.

tags.name: GateService
tags.description:
GateService grants the gates: shared resources, such as code generation (codegen), the local stack (stack), an
 end-to-end run (e2e) or a paid model run (paid), each held by one holder at a time, and granted only while the
 machine is not under pressure. To run a command under a gate: djinn gate run <name> -- <command>.

tags.name: CommandService
tags.description:
CommandService keeps what the commands of each project cost. Djinn measures each command a worker runs through
 djinn gate run: its CPU time, its peak memory and its duration, so that it learns what a project's usual commands
 cost.
